home.manifesto.label: Manifesto
home.manifesto.title: Artistic independence is a method, not a position.
home.manifesto.body1: Music is alchemy, and HISA is born where art, production and digital culture meet. Music is treated as experiment: a place to test ideas, dismantle formats and rebuild them with intention.
home.manifesto.body2: Knowledge circulates: studying becomes art, teaching becomes music, and music opens portals. Technology expands the gesture, never replaces it.
home.manifesto.principles.independence.t: No imposed formats. Each project defines its own rules of composition, release and scale.
home.manifesto.principles.experimentatio: Music as a field of research, where error belongs to the process and the result is never final.
home.manifesto.principles.tools.title: Technology as an instrument
home.manifesto.principles.tools.text: Software and machines are means of expression, not shortcuts, nor substitutes for an idea.
home.manifesto.principles.sharing.title: Shared knowledge
home.manifesto.principles.sharing.text: Production, teaching and mentoring belong to the same practice: creative autonomy.

music.label: Listen to HISA
music.title: HISA
music.bio1: HISA is a Brazilian singer, songwriter and music producer, born in Cuiabá, Mato Grosso. Her first form of expression was writing: as a child, she found in poetry and chronicles a place to translate what she could not say out loud. For nearly a decade she kept an anonymous blog where she shared her texts, some of them going viral without anyone knowing their authorship. At 16, she wrote the short story-poem “Oh, me”, which circulated online, mistakenly attributed to none other than Charles Bukowski. At 14, during a period of deep depression, she found in music a new possibility and began learning her first chords on the guitar and also producing her first beats on her own, exploring FL Studio and turning her computer into a limitless creative space. At 17, she moved to Curitiba, where she deepened her artistic training: she studied dance at the Escola de Dança Teatro Guaíra, voice and musical language and structuring at the Conservatório de Música Popular Brasileira (CMPB), and attended a few semesters of English Literature at UTFPR. It was also during this period that she began publishing covers regularly online, building her first international audiences after going viral on SoundCloud.
music.bio2: Her interest in the English language soon went beyond literature and began to guide her songwriting. Months after intensifying her studies of writing in English, she became a semi-finalist in the International Songwriting Competition. As Luiza Nis, she began an independent authorial trajectory, releasing works that bring together poetry, alternative pop, R&B and electronic experimentation. A graduate of Icon Collective Music School, HISA has developed a practice that crosses different dimensions of music creation: she writes, sings and produces both her own work and that of other artists. Among her collaborations is “Lilith”, by Bea Duarte, the singer's first major hit. Her authorial repertoire includes projects such as Parnasia (2017) and Levels, the Mixtape (2021), which surpassed 2.5 million organic streams, and A Noite Me Lava (2026). HISA represents the expansion of this trajectory: an artistic identity that brings together the sensibility of writing, the freedom of pop and the possibilities of a sound and technological universe in constant transformation. Artistically, her influences blend what is pop and mainstream with what is alternative and experimental: choruses are pop and almost metrically measured, while the verses can be lyrically and sonically experimental. In an interview at the release of her first EP, Parnasia, she said her inspirations range from Britney Spears to Tom Waits.
music.bio3: Beyond her own discography, HISA understands creation as a form of autonomy. One of the central purposes of her digital ecosystem is to widen access to education, technological tools and music production processes, especially for women and LGBTQIA+ people. In an industry where decision-making spaces and technical mastery remain deeply unequal, with men responsible for 96.8% of production credits in the sample analysed by USC Annenberg between 2012 and 2023, mastering creative tools also means claiming voice, independence and power over one's own narratives. Through music, education and creative experiences, HISA wants to contribute to a future in which more artists can not only take part in the industry, but understand, master and transform the means through which art is conceived.
